title: Never, Ma Soeur, Have I Loved You So Much...
text:
Never, ma soeur, have I loved you so much

as when I left you in that twilight.

The forest swallowed me, the blue forest, ma soeur,

over which the pale stars already remained forever in the west.


I did not laugh in the least, nothing at all, ma soeur,

I, who playfully walked toward my dark destiny—

while already the faces behind me

slowly grew pale in the dusk of the blue forest.


Everything was beautiful on that single evening, ma soeur,

and never again afterward; nor before—

of course only the great birds were left to me,

those that at evening are hungry in the dark sky.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated French address and the twilight departure toward dark destiny.

text:
It is no longer a slit-throat language, discord of symphonies, music


It is no longer a slit-throat language, discord of symphonies, music

of the

prodigy of a captured god. It is no longer.

Now everything defeats you, forgets you with

unction.

For you the ulcerated wine lies down, for you the wine of

childhood lies very cold


and its passion awakens, shadow in its judgments, in its instinct

whose perfumes

faint away. And while you go taking the eccentric form of my

vigil


I weep over a generation that is mine and does not exist. Over a generation

that does not exist and I sing it.

"Staff of Babel" 1982
editorial_note: The translation preserves Andreu's fractured syntax, repeated opening, and non-existent generation.

title: Love of Fires and of Perfection...
text:

It is no longer a slit-throat language, discord of symphonies, music

of the

prodigy of a captured god. It is no longer.

Now everything defeats you, forgets you with

unction.

For you the ulcerated wine lies down, for you the wine of

childhood lies very cold


and its passion awakens, shadow in its judgments, in its instinct

whose perfumes

faint away. And while you go taking the eccentric form of my

vigil


I weep over a generation that is mine and does not exist. Over a generation

that does not exist and I sing it.

"Staff of Babel" 1982
editorial_note: This alternate-title variant keeps the same Babel-fractured source text and opening ellipsis.

title: Take Off Your Hat...
text:
Take off your hat

if you have one

take off the hair

that abandons you

take off your skin

your guts your eyes

and put on a soul

if you find one.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Varela's stripping imperative and the stark final condition.

title: Weddings
text:
Lost in the fog,

the hummingbird and its lover.

Two stones hurled

by desire

meet in the air.

The broom is alive,

burning in the fog, inhabited.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the brief collision of desire and the living broom burning in fog.

title: That Is How It Must Be
text:
That is how the face of god must be,

heaven rabidly crossed

by gray, violet

and orange clouds,

and his voice

the sea below

always saying the same thing,

so monotonous,

so monotonous,

like the first

and the last day.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fierce sky-face and the sea's monotonous divine voice.

title: Dialogue
text:
He opens his mouth,

it is red inside.

She opens her eyes,

her cornea is white

like the moon.


It stays still,

the cornea moon,

barely illuminating

the well-beloved gum.


Inside,

with silence,

with mouth closed,

in the dark,

both dwell.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the bodily close-up and the silent interior where both figures dwell.

title: Soccer
text:
play with the earth

as with a ball


dance it

smash it

burst it


it is nothing but that, the earth,

you in the garden,

my goalkeeper, my scarecrow,

my Attila, my child.


the earth between your feet

turns as never before,

prodigiously beautiful.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the child's play with the earth as ball and beloved destructive beauty.

title: To Die a Little More Each Day
text:
To die a little more each day,

trim one's nails,

one's hair,

one's desires,

learn to think of the small

and the immense,

of the farthest

and motionless stars

in the sky

stained like an animal fleeing,

in the sky

frightened by me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the daily diminishment and the frightened, animal-like sky.

title: Story
text:
you can tell me anything

believing is not important

what matters is that the air move your lips

or that your lips move the air,

that you invent your story, your body,

at every hour, without truce,

like a flame that resembles nothing

but a flame.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the lower-case intimacy and the self-making flame.
